international_reference.title: A New Global Definition of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
key_rules: P/F = PaO2 divided by FiO2 fraction.
The Global ARDS definition uses P/F <=300 mmHg as one hypoxaemia criterion.
The Global ARDS definition permits S/F <=315 when SpO2 <=97%.
The oxygenation ratio alone is insufficient to establish ARDS because the definition contains additional criteria.

current_brazil_respiratory_surveillance.supersedes: Prior recommendations in the 2024 integrated Covid-19/influenza/other respiratory-virus surveillance guide and other previously applicable surveillance documents.
current_brazil_respiratory_surveillance.current_srag_definition_finding: The national SRAG surveillance case definition includes dyspnoea, tachypnoea and/or room-air SpO2 <=94% as deterioration criteria in a hospitalised patient with influenza-like syndrome.
current_brazil_respiratory_surveillance.oxygenation_engine_implication: This is a respiratory-surveillance case definition, not a replacement P/F or S/F formula and not a generic ARDS oxygenation definition.

conitec_review.catalog_freshness: Official PCDT catalog reviewed after its 2026-09-09 update.
conitec_review.finding: No general national P/F or S/F replacement calculation and no explicit formal SUS adoption statement for the 2023 Global ARDS definition were identified in the authoritative corpus reviewed for this audit.

historical_or_context_specific_brazil_ev.finding: Brazilian disease-specific and institutional documents may use P/F values in respiratory management pathways. Such use does not change the mathematical P/F ratio and must not be promoted to a generic national oxygenation calculator standard.

negative_finding_policy: no_national_variant_identified means no generic national variant was identified in the authoritative source corpus reviewed on the stated date; it is not a claim that no Brazilian publication can exist.
bh4b_implementation_rules: Preserve explicit FiO2 entry; do not infer FiO2 from oxygen flow or device labels.
Preserve the SpO2 >97% S/F caution and the Global ARDS applicability gate.
State explicitly that formal SUS adoption of the Global ARDS definition was not identified.
Do not reinterpret the national SRAG surveillance SpO2 <=94% criterion as an ARDS threshold.
Keep Brazilian surveillance context distinct from the international Global ARDS reference.
Repeat the Ministry/CONITEC/SBPT/AMIB source review at the final v2.0 release freeze.
